(u1, door_open) -> u2

(u2, at_goal) -> u3

feedback: Sound and compact encoding of the DoorKey achievement chain; accepted. (1) Semantic fidelity: u0->u1 on has_key, u1->u2 on door_open, u2->u3 on at_goal mirrors the mission and the three example tasks in order. The environment's constraints make this ordering forced (door_open requires the key in hand, at_goal requires passing the door), and pickup/toggle/forward are distinct actions, so the triggers cannot co-occur or fire out of order relative to the RM's state. (2) Regressions: none are required — the task is a chain of achievements ('eventually acquire the key', 'open after acquiring', 'reach after opening'), not a maintenance spec. Dropping the key does not negate prior achievements and re-pickup is always possible; the u1 else self-loop correctly absorbs key_lost and re-fired has_key with no reward. A re-shut door likewise leaves the RM in u2, and since a shut-but-unlocked door can be reopened without the key there is no deadlock. (3) Coverage: every state has an else self-loop, so irrelevant events (key_lost, repeated has_key/door_open firings) are absorbed; the u3 else self-loop provides post-terminal coverage. (4) Reward safety: rewards only on one-way progress transitions, all nonnegative, bounded (max total 1.2), with no backward transitions, so no reward-farming loops. (5) Format: matches the paper format; FINAL_STATES is nonempty, u3 is declared in STATES and is accepting (reached exactly on the terminal at_goal step, after which the episode ends). Minor non-blocking notes: rewards on else self-loops are implicit zero, which is conventional; the 0.1 reward for opening the door is modest relative to that milestone's exploration difficulty in the 16x16 variant — a slightly larger intermediate value would shape better, but this is tuning, not a fidelity defect.

feedback: The candidate defines exactly the four declared propositions and no extras. has_key matches the documented carrying check (carrying is not None, type 'key', color 'yellow') and is purely persistent. door_open matches the documented guarded grid scan for an open door; with a single door in DoorKey this is faithful. at_goal checks the single cell at env.agent_pos for a goal object, equivalent to the documented expression and purely persistent. key_lost correctly implements the declared event semantics: it reads the read-only previous_valuation snapshot (guarded for truthiness, no mutation, no writes to episode_memory), requires has_key true at the previous step, recomputes the current has_key and door_open conditions inline, and is true only on the drop step while the door is closed. At the first step prev['has_key'] is false, so key_lost is correctly false. All four functions contain no imports, no action calls, no side effects, and only read documented API members (env.carrying, env.grid.get, env.width, env.height, env.agent_pos, env.episode_memory). Python syntax is valid; return values reduce to booleans under truthiness in all branches. Boolean and temporal fidelity to the environment specification are preserved.
